messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: latency_slo_breach on /v1/stream (p95=1100ms, p99=2900ms) — increased tail latency and streaming stalls. Paging #incidents and @oncall.

Oncall (tess): Acknowledged. Im on-call, starting initial triage. Which stacks are firing?

Riley (sre): Seeing CPU saturation and long queues on preproc-tokenizer pods. p95 jump at 18:07 UTC. Traces show long waits in template-hydration -> tokenizer.encode.

Nina (runtime): Observed many requests hitting tool-schema expansion for dynamic tool lists. Some templates run expensive regexes during expansion. That plus JSON-mode heavy parsing seems to blow up worst-case cost.

Omar (ingest): Quick log snippet around 18:06: ```WARN prompt_hydrator: expand_tool_schema took 440ms, tokenizer.encode 1250ms, streaming_enqueue_wait 320ms, total_preproc 2.1s```

Jules (support): CS - Marco reports 6 customers saw stream disconnects and UI stalls between 18:05-18:12. One large enterprise saw multiple reconnects. Marco: customers on both hosted API and Dedicated pools.

Riley (sre): Triage hypothesis: high-cardinality templates causing repeated full-schema expansion and JSON-mode parsing on streaming hot-path. Amplified by simultaneous long templates causing a thundering-cache-miss effect.

Nina (runtime): Immediate mitigations I can apply: 1) flip global feature flag template_hydration_fast=false -> true to enable fast-path (tenant-scoped fallback) 2) disable JSON mode for streaming endpoints 3) apply emergency rate-limit for routes with >50 concurrent preproc ops.

Oncall (tess): Prioritize non-disruptive mitigations first. Can we disable JSON mode for streaming only?

Nina (runtime): Yes. Implementing now. Will also push a small patch that makes tool-schema expansion memcached for common fragments.

incident-bot: action:feature_flag_toggle user=Nina param=json_mode_streaming value=false  success.

deploy-bot: action:scale service=preproc-tokenizer from=5 to=12 triggered_by=Nina.

Omar (ingest): Scaling initiated. Also pinning HPA min replicas to 8 while we stabilize.

Riley (sre): After toggles and scale: p95 dropped to ~360ms, p99 ~720ms within 6 minutes. Streaming backpressure metrics improving. Still seeing isolated tails ~900-1100ms for huge templates.

Jules (support): Sending interim update to affected customers: "We're investigating increased streaming latency; temporary mitigations applied (disabled JSON streaming mode, scaled preproc). We'll follow up with root cause and ETA for permanent fix." :email:

CS - Marco: Please include whether Dedicated customers should expect any action on their end.

Nina (runtime): No action required from customers. We will re-enable JSON streaming once per-tenant gating and cache warming are in place.

Riley (sre): Creating incident ticket INC-2026-789 and assigning to runtime + ingest teams. Triage checklist: reproduce in perf test, identify regression window, list impacted tenants, implement cache-warming during deploys.

Omar (ingest): Noted an actionable pattern: when many requests include very long tool lists, the template hydrator does repeated string concatenation + regex parsing. We'll add a cheap length-based fast-path to skip full parse for >N items and return a truncated schema for streaming.

Nina (runtime): Follow-ups: memoize template expansion, add KV cache for common tool fragments, and implement a tokenizer "fast-encode" path that handles small/medium templates without heavy tokenization overhead. Estimate 48-72h to ship canary.

Riley (sre): Monitoring window set to 30m with threshold p99 < 800ms. If threshold breaks, escalate to eng-leads and paging rota.

Jules (support): Draft of final customer note ready; will send once we have a stable p99 and postmortem link.

deploy-bot: rolling_restart service=preproc-tokenizer shard=all initiated by=Nina.

Riley (sre): After rolling restart and cache priming, steady-state metrics: p95=320ms, p99=610ms, error rates back to baseline. No new customer error reports in last 20m.

CS - Marco: Thanks. Sending customer follow-up now.

Oncall (tess): Incident remains open until we have an RFC and a scheduled rollout with canary. Once RFC exists, move to postmortem state.

Nina (runtime): RFC created: "fast-paths for template hydration + tokenizer optimizations" assigned to eng-runtime with PRD. Reference: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-789

Riley (sre): Uploaded export of impacted tenant list and sample traces to /incidents/exports/3100000000/impacted_tenants.csv and /incidents/exports/3100000000/traces.json.

Jules (support): Confirmed customers notified and support channels monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to postmortem state. Postmortem owner: Nina. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-789

Riley (sre): Kudos team. Action items summarized in ticket: cache warming during deploy, per-route gating for JSON-mode, tokenizer fast-path, perf tests for worst-case templates.

Nina (runtime): Will schedule a canary next week and follow up on the RFC. Closing active paging. :thumbsup:"
